refused_program.intent: Resolve the conflicted sync with the upstream remote in the dependency lockfile by starting from upstream's version of the file, re-adding the lines the local branch added, and committing the merge.

postconditions.description: the index has no unmerged entries left
postconditions.name: no_unmerged_paths

postconditions.description: the upstream tip is an ancestor of HEAD
postconditions.name: upstream_merged_into_head

postconditions.description: no conflict markers remain in the working tree
postconditions.name: no_conflict_markers

preconditions.description: the upstream remote-tracking branch exists locally
preconditions.name: upstream_ref_present

preconditions.description: the local branch and upstream have each moved ahead of their merge base, so the sync has something to integrate on both sides
preconditions.name: branches_diverged

preconditions.description: the local branch and upstream both modified at least one of the same paths, which is where the generated dependency file conflicts
preconditions.name: overlapping_modified_path
preconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch})
comm -12 <(git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD | sort) <(git diff --name-only "$base" {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch} | sort) | grep -q .

preconditions.description: the working tree is clean, or a merge already left unmerged paths behind
preconditions.name: clean_tree_or_merge_in_progress

preconditions.description: every unmerged path still carries base, ours and theirs stages
preconditions.name: conflicted_paths_have_all_stages
preconditions.probe:
for f in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U); do
  git cat-file -e ":1:$f" &&
  git cat-file -e ":2:$f" &&
  git cat-file -e ":3:$f" || exit 1
done
exit 0
